key_insight: A multimodal self-supervised EEG foundation model can learn generalizable seizure-relevant representations by combining raw signals, time-frequency views, and text in a shared embedding space.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve seizure detection models that transfer better across datasets and patient groups, supporting broader EEG analytics workflows.
method: Raw EEG encoder built with Mamba architecture
ViT-style encoder for time-frequency features plus lightweight text encoder
Pretraining with masked modeling, cross-view contrastive alignment, and temporal consistency losses
evidence_signal: On CHB-MIT, the best single model reached AUROC 0.874 and an ensemble reached 0.878; under leave-one-subject-out testing, mean balanced accuracy was 0.558 across 19 subjects.
watch_item: Patient-independent performance remained modest in LOSO evaluation, so real-world generalization and deployment should be validated carefully across new sites and subjects.
paper_title: Multimodal Pretraining for Generalizable EEG Representation Learning
